titleEn: The Secret History of the Mongols — §§178–181: A Pail of Blood and a Round of Messages
part: §§178–181 — A Pail of Blood and a Round of Messages
about: Four sections, nearly all messages. In §178 Wang Qan, answering Chinggis's reproach, swears an oath: he cuts his little finger and sends the blood in a birch-bark pail 'to my son'. In §179 Chinggis sends word first to Jamuqa and then to Altan and Quchar, reproaching and reminding; §180 is his message to To'oril, a descent of slaves ending in Wang Qan's own name; §181 asks each of seven men for two envoys, brings Senggum's answer and ends with Arqai's report. The grammar is mostly converbs hung on one verb, plural commands in -dqun, and speeches inside speeches closed by keġen or keġežü. Several sentences here are hard, and the notes say where. The Mongol readings follow Shiratori; the English is a first drafting.

sentences.t: ede üges-tür Waṅ-Qān ügülerün:
sentences.l: These words-in, Waṅ-Qān speaking:
sentences.i: At these words Wang Qan said:
sentences.n: ügülerün is ügüle- 'speak' + -rün, the converb 'while speaking' that opens a speech (Ming 說); the colon after it tells you the words that follow are his. üges-tür is üge 'word' + the plural -s + -tür, 'in the words' (Ming 言語每 裏), here 'at these words': he is answering Chinggis's message of §177. Waṅ-Qān is Chinese wang 'prince' + qan.

morph.gloss: dative-locative: in, at (front-vowel form after s)
Wang Qan, ruler of the Kereid (Chinese wang 'prince' + qan; personal name) [人名]

sentences.t: "Ai! Soiluγ! köġün-eče-ġen qaγačaqu-ju töre-dēče qaγačaba.
sentences.l: "Ai! Soiluγ! Own-son-from parting-is?, custom-from parted.
sentences.i: "Alas! Am I parting from my own son? I have parted from what is right,
sentences.n: Ai! Soiluγ! is one printed word, two cries, glossed only (發喘) 'panting, gasping'. Wang Qan calls Chinggis 'son' (köġün), the mirror of Chinggis's 'father'; -ġen is the reflexive 'own', turned back on the speaker: köġün-eče-ġen 'from my own son'. qaγačaqu-ju is the participle qaγačaqu 'parting' + -ju; the Ming adds 麽, and in the published §§154-157 (ögkü-jü) and §§165-168 (žokiqu-ju) -ju after a participle is read as a question, so I take it so here: 'am I parting from my own son?'. The next pair, Hirižekü-jü ... hiričebe, has the same shape but the Ming 有 'is' instead of 麽, so I keep that one a plain statement; it could be a question too. töre is 'custom, order, what is right' (Ming 道理 'principle'); -dēče is the ablative, with Shiratori's long ē.

morph.gloss: cry of distress, 'alas' (interjection; the Ming gives only a sign of panting) [(發喘)]
a second cry beside ai (interjection; sense uncertain) [(發喘)]
to part, separate, break away [分離的 麽]
question particle after a participle (the Ming 麽; so -ju in §§154-157 and §§165-168)
custom, order, what is right (the Ming 道理 'principle') [道理 行]
ablative: from (written with Shiratori's long ē)

sentences.t: Hirižekü-jü üile-dēče hiričebe bi" keġen dura alžaγ̇ad ügülerün:
sentences.l: Estranging-is, from deed estranged, I," saying, heart distressed, speaking:
sentences.i: I am estranged; I have parted from the affair," he said, and with a troubled heart he went on:
sentences.n: The quotation closes on bi'; keġen is the converb 'saying'. Hirižekü-jü and hiričebe are one verb twice (Ming 分離 'separate'), the first the participle with -jü (as qaγačaqu-ju in the unit before; the Ming gives 有 'is' and no 麽, so I read it as a statement, but it may be a question), the second in the past; Shiratori writes ž in the first and č in the second. üile is 'deed, business' (Ming 勾當 'affair'); I leave 'the affair' unspecific, as the text does (the Ming 分離了 is simply 'parted'; the English says 'parted', not 'drifted'). The two quotations in this speech and the next unit are Shiratori's; this one closes on bi. dura alžaγ̇ad: dura 'heart'; alžaγ̇a- 'be distressed' is inferred from the Ming 艱難 'in difficulty', and the -d converb is uncertain.

morph.gloss: to part from, be estranged (written hiriže- here; the Ming 分離 'separate') [分離 有]
the same particle as -ju in qaγačaqu-ju (here the Ming 有 'is', not 麽; question or plain 'is', uncertain)
ablative: from (written with Shiratori's long ē)
to part from, be estranged [分離了]
to be distressed, be troubled (stem inferred from the Ming 艱難) [艱難︀了]

sentences.t: "Edöġe köġü-ben üžežü maγ̇ui sedkiġesü
sentences.l: "Now own-son seeing, bad if-thinking,
sentences.i: "Now, if I look on my son and think ill of him,
sentences.n: A conditional oath opens: -ġesü is 'if, when' (Ming 呵). The reflexive again, -ben, 'my own son'. The result clause is the next unit.

morph.gloss: son (a short form of köġün) [子 自的行]

sentences.t: ene metü čisu-ban γarγaγdasu" keġen andaγažü
sentences.l: this like own-blood be-brought-out-let," saying, oath-taking,
sentences.i: let my own blood be drawn out like this," he said, swearing an oath,
sentences.n: γarγaγdasu stacks three pieces on γar- 'go out': -γa- causative 'bring out', -γda- passive, -su the optative 'let it be' (Ming 者我), so 'let my blood be brought out'. ene metü, 'like this', points ahead to the act. andaγažü: the Ming 說誓 is 'say an oath'; the stem seems to come from anda 'sworn brother', and I read 'swearing', but that is uncertain.

morph.gloss: blood (the n lost before the ending) [血自的(行)]
reflexive-possessive: one's own (after a vowel, back-vowel form) [自的(行)]
optative: let it be (the Ming 者我)
to swear (brotherhood), take an oath (from anda; the Ming 說誓 'say an oath'; stem uncertain) [說誓着]

sentences.t: sigi-quruγ̇un-u-γ̇an toli onuči kituγai-bar qadqužu čisun čuburiγ̇ulžu
sentences.l: own little-finger's toli, notch-cutter knife-with, thrusting-in, blood making-drip,
sentences.i: stabbing his own little finger with a notch-cutting knife and letting the blood run,
sentences.n: Hard to read. The Ming glosses toli 指彈 'flicking the finger' and onuči 剜箭扣 'cutting an arrow-notch'. I take onuči as a knife for notching arrows (it stands before kituγai 'knife') and toli as some part of the finger, perhaps the tip; that is a guess. sigi-quruγ̇un: sigi Ming 小 'small', quruγ̇un Ming 指 'finger'; -u-γ̇an is genitive + reflexive 'own'. kituγai-bar is the instrumental, 'with a knife'. qadqužu and čuburiγ̇ulžu (čuburi- 'trickle' + causative 'make trickle'; Ming here 流出 'flow out') are -žu converbs, '-ing', that wait for the main verb ilebe a few units on.

morph.gloss: small (the Ming 小; uncertain) [小 指 自的(行)]
part of the finger, perhaps the tip (the Ming 指彈 'flicking the finger'; sense uncertain) [指彈]
notch-cutter (the Ming 剜箭扣 'cutting an arrow-notch'; uncertain) [剜箭扣]
instrumental: with (after a vowel, back-vowel form)
to trickle, flow in drops (the Ming here 流出 'flow out') [流出着]

sentences.t: üčüġüken daγtai-dur kižü
sentences.l: small birch-bark-pail-in, putting,
sentences.i: and putting it into a small birch-bark pail,
sentences.n: daγtai is Ming 樺皮小桶 'small birch-bark bucket'; -dur is the dative-locative, 'in'. kižü: the glossary's ki- is 'do, make', but the Ming here is 盛着 'filling, holding', so I read 'putting it in' (the blood into the pail); uncertain.

morph.gloss: small birch-bark pail (the Ming 樺皮小桶; stem uncertain) [樺皮小桶 裏]
to do, make; here 'put in, fill' (the Ming 盛 'hold, fill'; uncertain) [盛着]

sentences.t: "köġün-e min-u ög" keġežü ilebe.
sentences.l: "To-son my give," saying, sent.
sentences.i: "Give it to my son," he said, and sent it off.
sentences.n: ög is the bare stem of ög- 'give', a command; the quotation closes on it. ilebe: the Ming has 去了 'went', but ile- is 'send' elsewhere in the glossary, and with the pail and the speech just before, 'sent' fits better. Who carries the pail is not said, and nothing here says it reaches Chinggis.

morph.gloss: my, of me (bi, genitive stem min- + -u, set after its noun) [我的]
to give (the bare stem: a command, 'give!') [與]
to send (the Ming here reads 去了 'went') [去了]

sentences.t: Basa Čiṅgis Qaγan Žamuqa anda-da ügüle keġen ügülerün:
sentences.l: Again Chinggis Qaγan, to-Žamuqa to-sworn-brother, say, saying, speaking:
sentences.i: Again Chinggis Qahan sent word to his sworn brother Jamuqa, saying:
sentences.n: basa 'again' opens each message of this part. ügüle keġen ügülerün: ügüle is the bare stem 'say!', then 'saying', then 'speaking:'; it reads as the order 'tell (him)' that sends the words off, and then the words. Whether they are said in person or sent is not stated here, but §181 shows Chinggis working by envoys, so I read them as sent. anda is 'sworn brother'; Žamuqa anda-da: the two words are in apposition and the dative -da is written once, on the second.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]
Jamuqa, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
sworn brother, pledged friend [契交 行]
to speak, say (the bare stem: a command, 'tell (him)') [說]

sentences.t: "Qān ečige-dēče min-u üžen jadažu qaγačaγ̇ulba či.
sentences.l: "Qān father-from, my, seeing, unable, causing-to-part, you.
sentences.i: "You, unable to bear the sight, made me part from my father the Qan.
sentences.n: jada- after a converb means 'be unable to ...', so üžen jadažu is 'unable to see (me)'; Ming 見 不得着 is the Chinese idiom for 'cannot bear to see'. qaγačaγ̇ulba is qaγača- 'part' + the causative: 'made (him) part'. ečige-dēče is 'from father' with the long ē (the Ming 行 marks it as a case); the min-u after it is 'my', set after its noun as in Qān ečige-de min-u in §179 below, so 'from my father the Qan'. The one who is made to part is not named; I read it as the speaker ('made me part'). Nothing says whose sight Jamuqa could not bear, and I leave that open. či closes the sentence as subject, 'you', the Jamuqa addressed.

morph.gloss: qan, sovereign (the short form, before a kin term or after a name) [皇帝]
ablative: from (written with Shiratori's long ē)
my, of me (bi, genitive stem min- + -u, set after its noun) [我的]
to be unable (after a converb: unable to ...) [不得着]

sentences.t: Urida bosγsan bidan-u Qān ečige-jin kökö žüṅ uγ̇uqu büleġe.
sentences.l: Formerly risen, our Qān father's blue cup drinking there-was.
sentences.i: 'In the old days, when we had set out, we used to drink from the blue cup of Father Qan.
sentences.n: bosγsan bidan-u (Ming 起身的 咱的) is 'of us who rose, set out': the participle hangs on 'we', and I take it as 'we who set out in the beginning'. kökö žüṅ is 'blue cup' (Ming 靑 鍾); uγ̇uqu is the participle of 'drink', and büleġe 'there was' makes it a past habit, 'used to drink'.

morph.gloss: of us, our (bida 'we, inclusive', stem bidan-, + genitive -u) [咱的]
qan, sovereign (the short form, before a kin term or after a name) [皇帝]
past: there was, used to be

sentences.t: Na-da urida bosču uγdarun naidaba-že či.
sentences.l: To-me formerly rising, being-given-to-drink-when, envied-že you.
sentences.i: When I rose first and was served first, you were jealous of me.
sentences.n: The sense is that Chinggis, rising first, was served first, and Jamuqa begrudged it. uγdarun, Ming 被飮的 'being drunk, being given drink': it is uγ̇u- 'drink' (as in uγ̇uqu above) + the passive -γda- (the u lost: uγ-da-run) + -run 'when'; 'was served' is my reading of the passive, uncertain. na-da 'to me' goes with it. naida- 'envy, resent' (Ming 妒); -že 'indeed' (Ming 也者).

morph.gloss: to drink (as in uγ̇uqu above) [被飮的]
passive: be ...-ed (the u of the stem lost: uγ-da-); 'be drunk, be served'
to envy, resent (the Ming 妒 'be jealous') [妒了也者︀]

sentences.t: Edöġe Qān ečige-jin kökö žüṅ baradqun kedüi-že qoroqun ta" keġežü ilebe.
sentences.l: Now Qān father's blue cup drinking-up, how-much-že spending, you," saying, sent.
sentences.i: Now that you have drained the blue cup of Father Qan, how much have you wasted?" he said, and sent it.
sentences.n: baradqun carries -dqun, the plural-command ending (as in boludqun), but the Ming reads 飮了着 'having drunk', a converb; I follow the Ming, and cannot rule out a command ('drain it!'). qoroqun: the Ming 費的 'spending' reads like a participle, and with baradqun as a converb the sentence has no finite verb; 'have you wasted' supplies one, so the English is a guess at the sense. The Ming here is 費 'spend, waste', while the glossary's qoroqu- 'hold in the mouth' has a different Ming gloss, so this may be a different word. kedüi-že 'how much indeed' is rhetorical: how much of the Qan's bounty have you used up? ta, 'you', closes the sentence and the speech.

morph.gloss: qan, sovereign (the short form, before a kin term or after a name) [皇帝]
to finish, drain (stem inferred from the Ming 飮了 'drunk up') [飮了着]
ending of the plural command, which the Ming reads here as a converb 'having ...-ed' (uncertain)
how much, how many [幾多(也者︀)]
to waste, spend (the Ming 費 'spend'; the glossary's qoroqu- 'hold in the mouth' has another Ming gloss, so possibly another word) [費的]
to send (the Ming here reads 去了 'went') [去了]

sentences.t: Basa Čiṅgis Qaγan Altan, Qučar qojar-a ügüle keġen ügülerün:
sentences.l: Again Chinggis Qaγan, Altan, Qučar, to-the-two, say, saying, speaking:
sentences.i: Again Chinggis Qahan sent word to Altan and Quchar, the two, saying:
sentences.n: A second message in the same frame as the first. The two names stand in apposition to qojar-a, 'to the two' (dative -a, back-vowel form); the comma after Altan is Shiratori's.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]
Altan, a man's name (altan 'gold'; personal name) [人名]
Quchar, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
to speak, say (the bare stem: a command, 'tell (them)') [說]

sentences.t: "Ta qojar nama tebčižü ileġü-ü gesü keġeleġei ta;
sentences.l: "You two, me abandoning, face-to-face-ü, wanting-to-cast-off, did-you-say? you;
sentences.i: "Did you two say that you would cast me aside, openly, to my face?
sentences.n: keġeleġei: the Ming 說來麽 is 'did you say?'; the question is marked by the Ming's 麽, not by a letter. gesü, Ming 要弃 'wish to cast away': I take it as 'mean to (cast off)', but the stem is uncertain and could be a form of keġe- 'say'. ileġü-ü: Ming 對面 'face to face'; the final -ü has no gloss and I leave it an ending of uncertain force. nama is the stem of 'me' with no case ending (Ming 我行). tebčižü 'abandoning' and gesü (Ming 要弃) both carry 'cast off', and the English folds them into one verb; they may not be one act. This is an accusation, not a quotation I can place.

morph.gloss: two, the two (it follows the pair it counts) [兩箇]
me (the oblique stem of bi, with no case ending; the Ming 行 reads 'to, for me') [我行]
openly, face to face (the Ming 對面; uncertain) [對面]
an ending of uncertain force (the Ming glosses none)
to want, mean to (the Ming 要弃 'wish to cast away'; the stem may be a form of keġe- 'say'; uncertain) [要弃]
past ending of a question: did (you) ...? (the Ming 說來麽)

sentences.t: žüqažü-u gesü keġeleġei ta.
sentences.l: dealing-with-u, wanting-to-cast-off, did-you-say? you.
sentences.i: Did you say that you would cast me off by turning on me?
sentences.n: The same frame again, with žüqažü-u (Ming 對付着 'dealing with, coping with, confronting') for ileġü-ü. The stem žüqa- is uncertain and 'turning on' is my guess at the sense.

morph.gloss: to face, deal with, set against (the Ming 對付 'cope with'; stem uncertain) [對付着]
an ending of uncertain force (as -ü in ileġü-ü)
past ending of a question: did (you) ...?

sentences.t: Qučar-i čima-ji Nekün-Taiši-jin köġün keġežü
sentences.l: Qučar (acc), you (acc), Nekün-Taiši's son, saying,
sentences.i: Quchar, you, son of Nekün-Taishi: I said to you,
sentences.n: Two accusatives stand loosely before the saying that follows (keġežü ... kēġesü). Nekün-Taiši-jin köġün names who he is: 'Nekün-Taishi's son'. -jin is the genitive after a vowel.

morph.gloss: accusative: marks the object (after a vowel)
Nekün-Taishi, a man's name (personal name) [人名的]

sentences.t: bidan-ača či qān bol kēġesü ese bolba-že či.
sentences.l: from-us you qān become, if-said, not became-že you.
sentences.i: 'Be qan from among us,' and you would not.
sentences.n: kēġesü is 'if, when (one) says' (Ming 說呵); the subject, 'I' or 'we', is not stated. bol is the bare stem, 'become!'. ese bolba-že: ese negates the past; the Ming 不曾 肻做了 is 'would not agree to be'. So the plain reading is that Quchar was offered the title and refused. bidan-ača is bida 'we' + -n- + -ača 'from among us'.

morph.gloss: the stem-final n before a case ending
qan, sovereign (the short form, before a kin term or after a name) [皇帝]
to become, be (the bare stem: a command, 'become!') [做]

sentences.t: Altan-i čima-ji Qutula Qān-lu meden jabuluγ̇a
sentences.l: Altan (acc), you (acc), Qutula Qān-lu ruling went-about,
sentences.i: Altan, you: 'just as Qutula Qahan kept ruling,
sentences.n: -lu after Qān, Ming 但 'only, just', is uncertain (the ending -luγ̇a is 'with', which does not fit); I read 'just as Qutula Qan'. meden is the converb of mede- 'manage, rule' (Ming 管) and jabuluγ̇a is 'kept going', so the two together are 'kept ruling'. The sentence runs on into the next unit.

morph.gloss: accusative: marks the object (after a vowel)
Qutula, a man's name (personal name; also Qutula Qaγan) [人名]
particle after Qān (the Ming 但 'only, just'; uncertain)
to manage, rule (the Ming 管; stem uncertain) [管]
past ending of continuing action: kept ...-ing (uncertain)

sentences.t: ečige-jüġen meden aγsa- γ̇ar či qān bol kēġesü ese-kü bolba-že či.
sentences.l: own-father ruling going-by-way, you qān become, if-said, not-also became-že you.
sentences.i: and following the way your own father ruled, be qan,' I said; and you would not.
sentences.n: aγsa- and γ̇ar are one word split by the printer: aγsa-γ̇ar, with aγsa- Ming 往來的 'going and coming' (the stem inferred) and -γ̇ar the instrumental (Ming 依着 'following, according to'): 'in the way of his going'. ečige-jüġen is 'one's own father' (reflexive -jüġen). ese-kü is ese with kü 'also, even' (Ming 不曾 也); its force is uncertain and I translate 'would not'.

morph.gloss: to go about, travel (stem inferred from the Ming 往來 'going and coming'; the first half of aγsa-γ̇ar, split by the printer) [往來的]
instrumental: by, along, following (back-vowel form; the second half of aγsa-γ̇ar) [依着]
qan, sovereign (the short form, before a kin term or after a name) [皇帝]
to become, be (the bare stem: a command, 'become!') [做]
not (negates a past action) [不曾 也]

sentences.t: Deġe- re-eče Bartan-Baγ̇atur-un köġün keġežü
sentences.l: From-above Bartan-Baγ̇atur's sons, saying,
sentences.i: From above: the sons of Bartan-Ba'atur --
sentences.n: deġe- and re-eče are one word across a line: deġere-eče 'from above, from the upper side' (Ming 上 處). 'Of the senior line' would be my guess; the Ming says only 'from above'. Who the 'sons of Bartan-Ba'atur' are is not settled: the next unit names Sača and Taiču, whom §§43-54 give as sons of Qutuqtu-Yürki, not of Bartan, so the two phrases may be a looser pair than 'the sons, namely'. The English 'from above' keeps the Ming and does not say 'senior line'. Bartan-Baγ̇atur-un: -un after a consonant.

morph.gloss: above, upper (the first half of deġere-eče, split by the printer) [上]
ending of position: on the ... side (uncertain) [處]
Bartan-Ba'atur, a man's name (personal name; Ming 人名 勇士) [人名 勇士 的]

sentences.t: Sača, Taiču qojar-i ta qād boludqun keġežü jadaba-že bi
sentences.l: Sača, Taiču, to-the-two, you rulers become-you saying, unable-že I
sentences.i: I said to Sacha and Taichu, the two, 'Be sovereigns,' and I could not (bring it about)
sentences.n: boludqun is bolu- 'become' + -dqun, the plural command 'you all become!' (Ming 做您); qād is the contracted plural of qaγan, 'sovereigns' (the house rendering). keġežü jadaba-že bi: jada- after a converb is 'be unable to ...', so the plain grammar is 'unable to say'; the Ming reads 說着 不能了, 'saying, was unable'. I take it as 'I said it and could not carry it through (they declined)'. Which of the two is meant is uncertain.

morph.gloss: Sacha, a man's name (short for Sača-Beki; personal name) [人名]
Taichu, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
sovereign; the contracted plural qād, 'sovereigns' [皇帝每]
ending of the plural command: you (all) ... [您]
to be unable [不能了 也者︀]

sentences.t: tan-i qād boludqun keġežü jadažü
sentences.l: you (acc) rulers become-you saying, being-unable,
sentences.i: and to you too I said, 'Be sovereigns,' and could not (bring it about),
sentences.n: The same wording once more, now with tan-i, 'you' as object (tan- is the oblique stem of ta, 'you, plural polite'). Quchar and Altan are the 'you' of this message, as in the last two units.

morph.gloss: you (plural, polite; stem tan- before a case ending) [您行]
sovereign; the contracted plural qād, 'sovereigns' [皇帝每]
ending of the plural command: you (all) ...
-žu converb: -ing (written -žü here, though the stem is back-vowel)

sentences.t: tan-a či qān bol keġegdežü meden jabuba-že bi.
sentences.l: by-you you qān become being-told, ruling went-že I.
sentences.i: and being told by you, 'You be qan,' I went on ruling.
sentences.n: tan-a: the dative -a with a passive verb (keġegdežü 'being told') names who does the telling, 'by you'. The line of argument runs: when I could not make you rulers, you made me qan, and I ruled. meden jabuba-že, 'went about ruling' (Ming 管 行了).

morph.gloss: you (plural, polite; stem tan- before a case ending) [您行]
dative-locative: to, by (the doer of a passive; back-vowel form)

sentences.t: bu keġeġülüdkün; γurban müred-ün teriġün ken-e ber bu baγ̇uludqun" keġežü ilebe.
sentences.l: Not let-be-said-you; three rivers' head, to-anyone even, not, make-camp-you," saying, sent.
sentences.i: Do not let it be said of you; and let no one at all camp at the head of the three rivers," he said, and sent it.
sentences.n: Two prohibitions with bu 'do not', each closing on a plural command (-üdkün, -dqun). keġeġülüdkün is keġe- 'say' + -ġül- (causative; the Ming 被說 reads 'be told'): 'do not let it be said (of you)'. ken-e ber ... bu is 'to anyone at all ... do not': 'let no one'. baγ̇uludqun is baγ̇u- 'halt, settle' + causative, 'make (people) camp'. γurban müred-ün teriġün is 'the head of the three rivers' (Ming 三 河(每)的 源頭); the Ming names no rivers. The quotation closes here and ilebe ends the message.

sentences.t: Basa Čiṅgis Qaγan Toγ̇oril deġü-de ügüle keġen ügülerün:
sentences.l: Again Chinggis Qaγan, Toγ̇oril, to-younger-brother, say, saying, speaking:
sentences.i: Again Chinggis Qahan sent word to the younger brother To'oril, saying:
sentences.n: Toγ̇oril, glossed only 人名, is Wang Qan's own name; the printed text does not say so here, but the speech below addresses him and traces his line. deġü-de, Ming 弟 行 'to the younger brother', stands in apposition to Toγ̇oril (not 'as to a younger brother'); it is odd from Chinggis, who has called him father; the first words of the speech explain it: 'the reason for saying younger brother'.

To'oril, a man's name (personal name; here Wang Qan's own name) [人名]
to speak, say (the bare stem: a command, 'tell (him)') [說]

sentences.t: "Deġü keġekü josun Tumbinai, Čaraγal-Liṅγu qojar-un Oγda boγ̇ol(i)-γ̇ar bilažu irebe-že.
sentences.l: "Younger-brother saying reason: Tumbinai, Čaraγal-Liṅγu, the-two's Oγda as-slave seizing came.
sentences.i: "This is why I say 'younger brother': Oqda, of Tumbinai and Charaqai-Linggu, the two, came, carried off as a slave.
sentences.n: deġü keġekü josun, Ming 弟 說的 道理, is 'the reason for (my) saying 'younger brother''. What follows is a line of slaves, beginning with Oqda, taken as a slave by the two named men (presumably Chinggis's forebears; the speech ends by naming a high ancestor and a great-grandfather). The Ming 行 on boγ̇ol(i)-γ̇ar reads 'to slave'. qojar-un is a genitive, 'of the two', so the pair cannot be the subject; I read Oqda as the one who 'came', as the two's man, 'carried off as a slave' (the passive is mine: bilažu itself is active, 'seizing', and who seizes is not said). bilažu: Ming 擄着 'carrying off as plunder' (stem inferred). Charaqai-Linggu: Shiratori prints Čaraγal, probably a misprint of Čaraγai.

morph.gloss: custom, reason, the right way [道理]
Tumbinai, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
Charaqai-Linggu, a man's name (personal name; Čaraγal looks like a misprint of Čaraγai) [人名]

sentences.t: Jegei-Quṅtaγar-un köġün Toγ̇oril či ken-ü ulus-ud ögsü keġen žüšüridün jabuju. či.
sentences.l: Jegei-Quṅtaγar's son Toγ̇oril, you, whose people give-sü saying, flattering goes-about, you.
sentences.i: Jegei-Qungtaqar's son is To'oril, and you go about fawning, saying, 'Whose subjects am I to hand over?' — you.
sentences.n: The line ends on To'oril: Oqda, Sübegei, Kököchü-Kirsa'an, Jegei-Qungtaqar, To'oril, all of them slaves' sons. ken-ü ulus-ud ögsü: 'whose peoples let me give' (ögsü is the optative, Ming 與(呵)); žüšüridün jabuju 'is going about flattering' (Ming 諂佞 行有; žüšüri- inferred). The sense of the quoted question is not sure: handing over other men's subjects, or 'whom shall I serve and give (my people) to'. či closes the sentence a second time, 'you'.

sentences.t: Min-u ulus Altan, Qučar qojar ken-e ber ülü medeġülkün bijü-že.
sentences.l: My people Altan, Qučar, the two, to-anyone even, not make-rule-kün, is-že.
sentences.i: As for my people, Altan and Quchar, the two: no one is to be made their master.
sentences.n: My reading is shaky. The Ming runs 我的 百姓 / 人名 人名 兩箇 / 任誰行 也 / 不 / 敎管 / 有 也者, 'my people, Altan, Quchar, the two, to anyone also not make rule, is indeed'. medeġülkün is mede- 'manage' (Ming 管) + the causative + an ending -kün, which may be the plural command, so 'let none rule them'. Whether Altan and Quchar are in apposition to 'my people', or are those addressed, I cannot settle.

to manage, rule (the Ming 管) [敎管]

sentences.t: Čima-ji deġü keġekü josun borγai-jin min-u bosoγa-jin boγ̇ol elinčüġ-ün min-u eġüden-ü emčü boγ̇ol keġežü ilekü-ji min-u eimü.

sentences.i: The reason for calling you 'younger brother' is that you are the threshold-slave of my high ancestor, and the door's own slave of my great-grandfather." So saying, this is what I send.
sentences.n: It answers the opening of the speech: deġü keġekü josun again, then the reason. The pair sets the two men's births against each other; the Ming does not say whose side is the better, and I do not know the idiom (clothed at birth for good fortune? for rank?). ažuγ̇u-že: a- 'be', the past ending, -že.

sentences.i: Not letting go of the old feeling in my own heart,
sentences.n: üjen-ü: Ming 舊的 'old, former' (the stem is uncertain). sedkil(i)-jen: sedkil 'heart' + the reflexive -jen, Ming 心 自的行, 'my own heart'. talbin: talbi- 'put down, let go' (Ming 放) + converb. Chinggis says he has not given up his old regard for the Qan; the clause hangs on the next.

reflexive-possessive: one's own (front-vowel form; the (i) is Shiratori's) [自的行]

sentences.t: Qān ečige-ji amitu böġetele qān bolsu keġen
sentences.l: Qān father (acc) living while-being, qān let-him-be, saying,
sentences.i: 'so long as Father Qan lives, let him be Qan,' I say,
sentences.n: amitu 'living' (amin 'life' + -tu 'having'); böġetele, bü- 'be' + the converb -tele 'while, so long as' (Ming 有間). bolsu is the optative, 'let him be' (Ming 做).

morph.gloss: qan, sovereign (the short form, before a kin term or after a name) [皇帝]
accusative: marks the object (after a vowel) [行]

sentences.t: Qān ečige-jin bidan-u sedkil žoboγ̇ažu bu alγasaγ̇ul kēġed
sentences.l: Qān father's our heart suffering, not make-divide, having-said,
sentences.i: and 'do not let the heart of our Father Qan suffer and be torn,' saying,
sentences.n: bu alγasaγ̇ul, 'do not make (it) part' (Ming 休 敎分了): alγasa- 'split' (Ming 分) + the causative as a bare command. Chinggis gives two commands, bolsu keġen 'let him be qan' and bu alγasaγ̇ul kēġed 'do not let it be torn'. kēġed is keġe- + -ġed 'having said', with the long ē. žoboγ̇ažu is Ming 生受着 'suffering', without the 敎 'make' of žoboγ̇an above; I read 'being in hardship'.

morph.gloss: qan, sovereign (the short form, before a kin term or after a name) [皇帝]
of us, our (bida 'we, inclusive', stem bidan-, + genitive -u) [咱的]
to suffer hardship (the Ming 生受 'suffer', without the 敎 of žoboγ̇an above; uncertain) [生受着]
to part, split, divide (the Ming 分) [敎分了]

sentences.t: Seṅgüm anda na-dur elči ile.
sentences.l: Seṅgüm sworn-brother, to-me envoy send.
sentences.i: Senggum, my sworn brother, send an envoy to me.
sentences.n: ile is the bare stem of ile- 'send', a command (Ming 敎來 'cause to come'). elči 'envoy' (Ming 使臣).

morph.gloss: to send (the bare stem: a command, 'send!') [敎來]

sentences.t: Irerün Bilge-Beki, Tödöġen qojar-un nököd-i ile" keġežü ilebe.
sentences.l: When-coming Bilge-Beki, Tödöġen, the-two's companions (acc) send," saying, sent.
sentences.i: When he comes, send the companions of the two, Bilge-Beki and Tödögen," he said, and sent it off.
sentences.n: irerün 'when coming' (-rün; Ming 來時). Whose companions: the Ming 人名 人名 兩箇 的 伴當(每)行 is 'the two's companions', the companions of Bilge-Beki and Tödögen; whether Chinggis wants them returned, or to travel with the envoy, I cannot tell. nököd is the plural of nökör 'companion, follower' (-i accusative). The quotation closes on ile; the sentence goes on keġežü ilebe, 'saying, sent', and again no object is given for ilebe ('sent it' means the message).

morph.gloss: Bilge-Beki, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
Tödögen, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
to send (the bare stem: a command, 'send!') [敎來]
to send (the Ming here reads 去了 'went') [去了]

sentences.t: "Na-dur elčin irerün Qān ečige qojar elčin ile.
sentences.l: "To-me envoys when-coming, Qān father two envoys send.
sentences.i: "When envoys come to me, Father Qan, send two envoys.
sentences.n: A new quotation opens (Shiratori's mark), and now the message is a roll-call, repeated for each man in the same few words. elčin is a form of elči 'envoy'. qojar elčin, 'two envoys' (Ming 兩箇 使臣): here the numeral stands before its noun.

morph.gloss: envoy, messenger (a form of elči) [使臣]
qan, sovereign (the short form, before a kin term or after a name) [皇帝]
to send (the bare stem: a command, 'send!') [敎來]

sentences.t: Seṅgüm anda qojar kü elčin ile.
sentences.l: Seṅgüm sworn-brother, two also envoys send.
sentences.i: Senggum, my sworn brother, send two envoys also.
sentences.n: kü is 'also, indeed' (Ming 也); each name after the first takes it.

morph.gloss: to send (the bare stem: a command, 'send!') [敎來]

sentences.n: The same roll-call; Jamuqa is anda here as in §179.

morph.gloss: to send (the bare stem: a command, 'send!') [敎來]

sentences.l: Qačiγ̇un, two also envoys send," saying.
sentences.i: Qachi'un, send two envoys also," he said.
sentences.n: The last of the roll: Father Qan, Senggum, Jamuqa, Altan, Quchar, Achiq-Shirun, Qachi'un. The quotation closes on ile and keġen 'saying'.

morph.gloss: Qachi'un, a man's name (a son's name; personal name) [人名]
to send (the bare stem: a command, 'send!') [敎來]

sentences.t: Arγai-Qasar, Sügegei-Žeġün qojar(i)-jar edüi üges daγ̇u bariγ̇ulužu ilebe.
sentences.l: Arγai-Qasar, Sügegei-Žeġün, by-the-two, this-much words, message making-hold, sent.
sentences.i: He sent off Arqai-Qasar and Sükegei-Jegün, the two, to carry these words as his message.
sentences.n: qojar(i)-jar is the instrumental, 'by means of the two' (Ming 兩箇(依著)): the two are the means by which the words go. daγ̇u 'voice, message' (Ming 聲); bariγ̇ulužu is bari- 'hold, take' + the causative, 'having them carry', as in daγ̇u bariγ̇ulurun in §177. edüi 'this much' (Ming 只這般).

morph.gloss: Arqai-Qasar, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
Sükegei-Jegün, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
instrumental: by means of (the (i) is Shiratori's) [(依著)]
so much, this much (the Ming 只這般) [這些]
voice, word, message (the Ming 聲 'voice') [聲話]
converb: -ing (-žu after a linking u; back-vowel form)
to send (the Ming here reads 去了 'went') [去了]

sentences.t: Ede üges ein ügülegdežü Seṅgüm ügülerün:
sentences.l: These words thus being-said, Seṅgüm speaking:
sentences.i: When these words had been said to him in this way, Senggum said:
sentences.n: ügülegdežü is ügüle- + passive + converb, Ming 被說着 'being said'; the words are those the two envoys brought.

sentences.t: "Keli Qān ečige keġekü büleġe;
sentences.l: "When Qān father saying there-was;
sentences.i: "Whenever he spoke, it was 'Father Qan';
sentences.n: I read keli, Ming 幾時, as 'whenever, at any time', and Qān ečige keġekü büleġe as 'he used to say 'Father Qan'' (Senggum is the speaker, introduced by ügülerün: just before; 'he' is Chinggis, who is not named). This and the next three units are hard, and I give only a tentative reading: that Senggum is saying Chinggis's fair words are not to be trusted.

morph.gloss: when, at any time (the Ming 幾時 'when'; uncertain) [幾時]
qan, sovereign (the short form, before a kin term or after a name) [皇帝]
past: there was, used to be

sentences.t: kiduγ̇ači ebügen ese-ü keġekü büleġe.
sentences.l: Killer old-man not-? saying there-was.
sentences.i: did he not say 'the old killer'?
sentences.n: kiduγ̇ači, Ming 好殺的 'fond of killing' (the stem is uncertain); ebügen 'old man'. ese-ü is ese 'not' + the question particle, 'did he not ...?' (the Ming 麽 stands only on the second ese-ü keġekü büleġe, 473, and not here, so this one may be a plain statement, 'he never said ...'). I read it as Senggum charging that Chinggis privately called the Qan an old killer; tentative.

morph.gloss: one fond of killing, a killer (the Ming 好殺的; stem uncertain) [好殺︀的]
past: there was, used to be

sentences.t: Nama keli anda keġen büleġe.
sentences.l: To-me when sworn-brother saying there-was.
sentences.i: And to me, whenever, it was 'sworn brother'.
sentences.n: The same keli as above and keġen büleġe, 'was saying' (Ming 麽道 有來). Whenever Chinggis spoke to Senggum it was 'anda', on this reading.

morph.gloss: me (the oblique stem of bi, with no case ending; the Ming 行 reads 'to, for me') [我行]
past: there was, used to be

sentences.t: Toγtoγ̇a böġe Sartaγčin qonin-u seġül žübčižü jabuju.
sentences.l: Toγtoγ̇a shaman Sartaγčin sheep's tail attaching goes-about.
sentences.i: Toqto'a the shaman, the Sartaqchin, goes about adding on to the sheep's tail.
sentences.n: Joining-on is žübčižü, Ming 續着 'continuing'; the 'himself' of an earlier draft is not in the text. I do not know what this refers to; the Ming offers only 師公 'shaman' for böġe, 囘囘 'Muslim' for Sartaγčin, and 羊的 尾子 續着 'continuing / adding on the sheep's tail'. It reads like an example or a saying (hanging on at the tail of a flock), and I give the words rather than a sense. Toγtoγ̇a is the same name as in earlier parts.

morph.gloss: Toqto'a, a man's name (personal name) [(人)名]
Sartaqchin, a Muslim or a Muslim group (the Ming 囘囘; sense uncertain) [囘囘]
to attach, continue, join on (the Ming 續 'continue') [續着]
converb -žu written with j, standing as a finite 'is ...-ing' (uncertain)

sentences.t: ese-ü keġekü büleġe.
sentences.l: Not-? saying there-was.
sentences.i: Did he not say so?
sentences.n: ese-ü keġekü büleġe, 'did he not say?'; the Ming 麽 marks the question. What 'so' is, the unit before leaves open.

morph.gloss: past: was (the Ming 麽 marks a question)

sentences.t: Edeġer üges-ün arγas uqaγdaba."
sentences.l: These words' schemes perceived-were."
sentences.i: The schemes in these words have been perceived."
sentences.n: edeġer is the plural of ede 'these'. arγas is arγa 'means, plan' + plural (Ming 計量 'calculations'); uqaγdaba is uqa- 'perceive' (Ming 覺) + passive + past, 'was perceived'. Shiratori prints a closing quotation mark here, though the speech seems to go on in the next unit; I follow his mark and open a new quotation in the next unit, which he does not mark.

morph.gloss: means, plan, scheme (the Ming 計量 'calculation') [計量]
to understand, perceive (the Ming 覺) [可覺了]

sentences.t: Qadqulduγ̇an-u teriġüd üges bi.
sentences.l: "Fighting's heads words is.
sentences.i: "The first words of the fighting are these:
sentences.n: qadqulduγ̇an-u teriġüd üges bi, Ming 厮殺的 頭每 言語每 有: 'the chiefs' (or first) words of the fighting are'. teriġüd is the plural of teriġün 'head, first'; whether 'chiefs' or 'first' is meant, I do not know. bi 'is' (Ming 有). No opening quotation mark is printed here.

morph.gloss: is, there is (perhaps a short form of bü-) [有]

sentences.t: Bilge-Beki, Tödöġen qojar qadqulduqui tuγ bosγadq̇un: aγtas tarγulaγ̇uludqun; arijal ügei bi-že" keġebe.
sentences.l: Bilge-Beki, Tödöġen, the-two fighting standard raise-you; geldings fatten-you; doubt without is-že," said.
sentences.i: Bilge-Beki and Tödögen, you two, raise the battle standard; fatten the geldings; there is no doubt," he said.
sentences.n: Three plural commands (-dqun): bosγadqun 'raise' (Ming 立起您) the tuγ, the standard (Ming 旄纛); tarγulaγ̇uludqun 'make fat' the geldings (aγtas; Ming 肥, stem inferred), that is, get the war-horses ready. arijal ügei bi-že, 'doubt there-is-not indeed': no doubt. keġebe 'said'; the speaker is still Senggum, I take it. Bilge-Beki and Tödögen are the two whose companions Chinggis asked for in the message above.

morph.gloss: standard, banner (the Ming 旄纛) [旄纛]
ending of the plural command: you (all) ...
to grow fat (from tarγun 'fat'; stem inferred from the Ming 肥) [敎肥了您]
ending of the plural command: you (all) ...

sentences.t: Tedüi Waṅ-Qān-(n)ača Arγai-Qasar qariqui-dur Sügegei-Žeġü- n-ü eme köġün tende Toγ̇oril-dur ažuγ̇u.
sentences.l: Thereupon from-Waṅ-Qān Arγai-Qasar returning-at, Sügegei-Žeġün's wife son there with-Toγ̇oril was.
sentences.i: Then, as Arqai-Qasar was coming back from Wang Qan, the wife and son of Sükegei-Jegün were there with To'oril.
sentences.n: tedüi 'then, thereupon' (Ming 卽便); Waṅ-Qān-(n)ača 'from Wang Qan' (ablative, with Shiratori's (n)); qariqui-dur is qari- 'return' + -qui + -dur, 'at the time of returning'. Sügegei-Žeġü- and n-ü are the name Sügegei-Žeġün + -ü split by a line break: 'of Sükegei-Jegün'. eme köġün is Ming 妻 子, 'wife (and) son', two persons; I read it so without grammar to prove it. Toγ̇oril-dur 'with To'oril'. Waṅ-Qān and Toγ̇oril are here in one sentence for the same man.

morph.gloss: so, then, thereupon (the Ming 卽便) [卽便]
ablative: from (back-vowel form; the (n) is Shiratori's) [處]
dative-locative: at the time of (back-vowel form)
Sükegei-Jegün, a man's name (the first half, printed Sügegei-Žeġü-, the n carried to the next word by the line break) [人名]
the end of Sügegei-Žeġün-ü: genitive: of (front-vowel form) [的]
To'oril, a man's name [人名 行]

sentences.t: Odqu žürüge jadažu Sügegei-Žeġün, Arγai-(j)ača qočorčuγ̇ul.
sentences.l: Going heart unable, Sügegei-Žeġün, from-Arγai lagged-behind.
sentences.i: Unable to bring himself to go, Sükegei-Jegün fell behind Arqai.
sentences.n: odqu žürüge jadažu, 'going, heart, unable' (Ming 去的 心 不能着): his heart could not go, and the unit before it gives the reason. qočorčuγ̇ul: Ming 落後了有 'has lagged behind'; I take qočor- as the stem and -čuγ̇ul as a past ending of the family of -žuγ̇u (uncertain). Arγai-(j)ača 'from Arqai' (the (j) is Shiratori's).

morph.gloss: Arqai, a man's name (short for Arγai-Qasar) [人名 行]
ablative: from (back-vowel form; the (j) is Shiratori's) [行]
to be left behind, lag (stem inferred from the Ming 落後) [落後了有]
past ending, perhaps a variant of -žuγ̇u (the Ming 了有; uncertain)

sentences.t: Araγai irežü ede üges Čiṅgis Qaγan-(n)a ügülebe.
sentences.l: Araγai coming, these words to-Chinggis Qaγan spoke.
sentences.i: Arqai came and told these words to Chinggis Qahan.
sentences.n: Araγai is spelled with an extra a here, but the Ming 人名 and the context make him Arγai-Qasar. ügülebe 'spoke' (past -be) is the verb the whole run of messages has been waiting for. Qaγan-(n)a: the dative -(n)a, with Shiratori's (n).

morph.gloss: Arqai, a man's name (Arγai-Qasar, spelled with an extra a) [人名]
Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]
